options.title: Adidas and Puma Were One Shoe Company, Run by Two Brothers
options.first_line: Adidas and Puma were one shoe company, run by two brothers.
options.first_frame: Puma's annual report page with its sales figure highlighted in yellow, the Adidas and Puma logos side by side on it; then a cut to an Adidas and a Puma shoe.

options.title: Two Brothers Split One Shoe Factory Into Adidas and Puma
options.first_line: Two brothers split one shoe factory in half, and made Adidas and Puma.
options.first_frame: A typeset report card with the year's sales line highlighted, under the two logos; then a cut to the river running through their small German town.

options.title: Adidas and Puma Grew Up on Opposite Banks of One River
options.first_line: Adidas and Puma grew up on opposite banks of one small river.
options.first_frame: A report page highlighted on the sales line with both logos, then a cut to the little river in Herzogenaurach.

why: Two brands the viewer wears, shown as one company, makes a stranger ask how it broke into rivals without the title giving away the split, and the cut to the two shoes says it all with the sound off.
